sōl, sōlis m.

noun, third declension

The sun in the sky; for its light and warmth, see sunshine. Sōl oriēns and sōl occidēns, the rising and the setting sun, are also the east and the west (Caes. BG 1.1).

Examples

  • Quid potest esse sōle majus?

    What could be bigger than the sun?Cic. Ac. 2.82 (Lewis & Short)

  • mox diēs vērus; sōl etiam effulsit

    then real daylight; the sun even shone outPlin. Ep. 6.20.18

  • Salvē, sōl! Grātiās agō prō nuce pīneā, et prō bacillō, et prō elephantīs avī!

    Hello, sun! Thank you for the pine cone, and for the stick, and for Grandpa’s elephants!Libellus IV, Diēs Grātulātiōnis

See also sunshine, sunny, sunrise, sunset, sky, moon.

SourcesLewis & Short: sol

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 387.
